2610.10049.title: The Long Road to the Same Answer: Cognitive Bias Under Escalating Reasoning Budgets in Large Language Models
2610.10049.paper_summary: Reasoning models allocate extra computation at inference time and present their answers as the product of deliberate thought. If this deliberation works the way dual-process accounts of human cognition suggest, longer thinking should weaken the classic decision biases that fast, intuitive judgment produces. Using 30 vignettes covering six biases (anchoring, framing, loss aversion, escalation of commitment, availability, confirmation) from an established benchmark, we run a dose-response study across four model families, pairing each reasoning model with a matched non-reasoning sibling and requesting thinking ceilings of 0, 1,024, 4,096, and 8,192 tokens, for 12,350 API calls. Because a requested ceiling is not the same as realized deliberation, we use the reasoning tokens each call consumed as the dose. First, reasoning models are not less biased than their siblings; the point estimate leans the other way in every family, but the item-level pooled contrast is not reliable (Delta = +0.031, t(29) = 1.45, p = .157). Second, bias magnitude does not reliably fall as realized deliberation grows: no slope is significantly negative, and where anything moves it is the signed score drifting further from the human direction. Third, anchoring is the only bias in the human direction (d = 1.89). Four of the other five lean the opposite way in all seven models; with five items per bias, that reversal is reliable for framing and directional for escalation of commitment, confirmation, and loss aversion, while availability is absent. A one-line instruction to restate the anchor before answering lowered anchoring on all five anchoring items, which no amount of additional thinking did, although the effect does not reach significance (p = .057). The results argue against treating test-time reasoning as a rationality guarantee and for auditing deployed models bias by bias.
2610.10049.paper_summary_zh: 推理模型在推理時分配額外的計算資源，並將其答案呈現為深思熟慮的結果。<lb/>如果這種深思熟慮的過程如雙過程理論所暗示的那樣運作，則較長的思考應該會減弱快速直覺判斷所產生的經典決策偏差。<lb/>我們使用涵蓋六種偏差（錨定、框架、損失厭惡、承諾升級、可得性、確認）的30個小插曲，進行了一項劑量反應研究，跨越四個模型家族，將每個推理模型與一個匹配的非推理兄弟配對，並要求思考上限為0、1,024、4,096和8,192個標記，共進行12,350次API調用。<lb/>由於請求的上限與實際的深思熟慮並不相同，我們使用每次調用消耗的推理標記作為劑量。<lb/>首先，推理模型的偏差並不比其兄弟少；每個家族的點估計都向相反方向傾斜，但項目級的合併對比並不可靠（Delta = +0.031，t(29) = 1.45，p = .157）。<lb/>其次，隨著實際深思熟慮的增長，偏差的大小並不可靠地下降：沒有斜率顯著為負，而在任何變動的地方，簽名分數都在進一步偏離人類的方向。<lb/>第三，錨定是唯一向人類方向的偏差（d = 1.89）。<lb/>其他五種偏差在所有七個模型中都向相反方向傾斜；每種偏差有五個項目，這種反轉在框架上是可靠的，並且在承諾升級、確認和損失厭惡上是有方向性的，而可得性則缺席。<lb/>在回答之前重述錨定的一行指示降低了所有五個錨定項目的錨定，這是額外思考無法做到的，儘管該效果未達到顯著性（p = .057）。<lb/>這些結果反對將測試時的推理視為理性保證，並支持逐偏差審計已部署模型的偏差。
